rationale: Review of the first artifact of the new obligation c-snapshot-restore-commit-context (artifact 32d511373b4a46d9a7d55597b3e632f0, version 1), which the trusted runner executed as check 6c982b1fcb114ff7b3e4b22ace5a238b. The run reproduced the violation on the recovery path: the node reported index 43 as committed, applied and last before the restart, the restart restored that snapshot (restored true, last_snapshot_index 43), and the restarted node then published commit_index 0 through Raft.CommitIndex() while applied_index and last_index were 43 and Stats published commit_index 0 beside applied_index 43. The artifact's contract requires a checker_correspondence item, which this product supplies together with an applicability item. No review issue is open for this target, so no resolution is carried.

review_items.rationale: The obligation under review says that a node reconstructing its state at startup from a stored snapshot at index J must publish a commit context at least J, because the exported accessor is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation. The encoded proposition is one comparison: the commit index the restarted node publishes must equal the admitted index, which the same node reported as committed, applied and last before the restart and which the stored snapshot covers. Equality is not a stronger predicate here: the restarted node's own last index is the admitted index, and a follower's commit index is otherwise only ever set to min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), so no legal value could exceed it and equal-to-J and not-below-J coincide inside this prefix. The fixed entry is the module's own construction path: NewRaft scans the log, restoreSnapshot restores the newest stored snapshot and publishes lastApplied, lastSnapshot, the committed configuration and the latest configuration from it, and the harness only reads through public accessors; the snapshot it restores is one the same node produced through the public Snapshot API, so the compared index is an index that node had committed and applied. The oracle is the monitor's comparison on the retained events rather than the test: the harness prints raw fields and exits zero, and the checker reported violated on exactly the correlated pair. Identity is sound: both events carry the same node and op identity, the admission alias selects snapshot_committed_before_restart, the result event is selected by the operation and the admission precedes it in the single retained stream. The legal history is visible in the record: snapshot_committed_before_restart reports index 43, term 2 and commit, applied and last indexes of 43; restore_context_observed reports restored true, last_snapshot_index 43 and snapshot_index 43, so the node itself reports the restore of that exact snapshot, together with commit_index 0, applied_index 43, last_index 43, stats_commit 0, stats_applied 43 and state Follower. Completion is established rather than assumed: the second Raft instance is constructed only after the first one's Shutdown returned, and the construction path restores the snapshot synchronously before NewRaft returns, so the read that produces the result event happens after the restore has completed; the restored flag taken from the node's own last-snapshot report is what gates applicability. Counterevidence is explained in the rationale rather than left standing: the map's min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex) describes the append path, not construction from stores; no source states that the value is intended to stay zero on this path, and no source states that it is meant to be derived from the last snapshot index either, so the repair location remains open as recorded; the election timers of the restarted instance are long only so that nothing campaigns between construction and the read, which does not change what construction published. What the check does not establish is listed in limitations.
limitations: The observation is taken immediately after construction, so it does not measure how long the value stays low before a leader contacts the node or the node campaigns.
The restart keeps the log entries the snapshot covers because TrailingLogs is left large, so a configuration that had compacted them away is not exercised.
The equality encoding coincides with 'not below the admitted index' only because the restarted node's own last index is the admitted index inside this prefix.
The check reports the published index only; no in-repo consumer was exercised that misbehaves because of the low value.
review_items.report_title: 重启恢复快照后提交索引仍为零
review_items.report_answer: 受信运行复现：重启前该节点把索引 43 报告为已提交、已应用且为最后索引；重启后 restored 为 true、last_snapshot_index 与 snapshot_index 均为 43，但通过 Raft.CommitIndex() 发布的 commit_index 为 0，而 applied_index 与 last_index 均为 43，Stats 同样给出 commit_index 0，检查器裁定 violated。该前缀中重启节点自身最后索引即被承认的索引，因此等值判断与“不低于”在本范围内一致；本检查不测量该值保持为零的时长。

review_items.rationale: The implementation owes this responsibility in the selected scope because the node has itself reconstructed and applied committed state at startup, and the value it publishes is the library's own answer to the question the requirement names. restoreSnapshot publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the stored snapshot index and rebuilds the committed and latest configurations, but it never writes the commit index, which is otherwise written only in the appendEntries commit branch as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex); the node therefore publishes zero for an index it reports as applied and as its last snapshot. The declared meaning of the fact is not satisfied on this path either: the snapshot the node restores was taken by the same node through takeSnapshot after it had applied and committed through that index, so the entries it covers are stored by a quorum of the configuration the snapshot carries, which is what the fact asserts for a commit index. The exported accessor is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation, so a caller on a restarted node cannot derive a read index for the committed state that node has just restored, and Stats publishes the same value beside the applied index and the snapshot index it contradicts. The check exercises the duty on the module's own construction path with the node's own snapshot, so the obligation binds the shipped recovery path and not only the harness. The alternatives are answered rather than left standing: reading the zero as 'no commit index has been advertised yet' does not fit a node that has restored and applied the committed state and reports that snapshot index itself, and treating the omission as deliberate would require a source saying so, which none provides; the sibling runtime path already accepted the same duty, which is why this entry point is stated separately and not merged into that prefix.
limitations: The duty is established for the construction-time restore of a snapshot the same node produced; restoring a snapshot received from another node and the runtime install path remain separate entry points.
The consequence claimed is a client-contract one; no consumer outside the module was available to demonstrate a downstream failure.
The repair location stays open between advancing the commit index during the restore and deriving the published value from the last snapshot index.
review_items.report_title: 该发布义务覆盖启动时的快照重建路径
review_items.report_answer: 该节点在启动时已把快照承载的状态重建并应用，而发布该值的正是库自身的导出访问器与 Stats；跟随者的提交索引在别处仅由 appendEntries 按 min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex) 写入，因此该义务约束随库附带的恢复路径。把该零值解释为“尚未收到提交索引”与节点自身恢复并应用了已提交状态这一事实不符；本义务与运行时安装路径分别陈述，未合并进同一前缀。
